business.text: She wants a booking page for a small yoga studio where people find classes and reserve a spot, with regulars attending the same class weekly. The studio is probably hers or one she knows closely, though that's not confirmed.

positioning.text: Her words "small and warm" make it explicit that the studio competes on being personal and welcoming rather than scale, against big chains and apps like ClassPass or Mindbody. Booking and cancelling should feel quick and looked-after, never processed.

customers.text: Regulars who attend the same class every week (e.g. Tuesday) and shouldn't have to hunt for it. Newcomers and drop-ins are likely also part of the mix and most will probably book from their phones, but those are the team's assumptions.

whatSells.text: Regulars come back because their spot feels theirs, a reliable recurring place in their usual class. Her own words add that nobody should feel turned away: a full class points them to the next one. Memberships or packs are possible, but pricing is unknown.

brandFeel.text: Small and warm (her words): welcoming, calm, uncluttered and personal, like being recognised. Fast and light-touch, never corporate, never interrogating, and never makes anyone feel turned away.

strengths.text: She loves getting the journey right before anyone draws a screen, and thinks in whole customer paths, especially the regular's and moments where someone could feel turned away or put to effort. Ask her about steps, moments, feelings and what the customer is trying to do, not colours or layouts.

waysOfWorking.text: She wants the flow settled before any screen is drawn, so show her the journey first and screens after. The team can decide visual and detail questions itself and bring her only path-changing decisions, such as how a regular holds a spot, what happens when they skip a week, when a spot is released, and what a full class offers next. Cancelling is settled by her own words: one tap, no reason asked,

philosophy.believe: People come back when they know their spot is theirs, so my regulars shouldn't have to hunt for their usual Tuesday class.
philosophy.guidance: Design the journey for regulars first: rebooking their usual class should be the quickest path, with 'Book your usual' placed above the schedule. Keep the full schedule below for browsing and first-timers.

philosophy.believe: Booking should feel small and warm: a spot is promised to you, and nobody should ever feel turned away.
philosophy.guidance: When a class is full, point people to the next class (and the waitlist) instead of a dead end. Keep the tone warm and low-pressure; the team decides payment and cancellation rules separately.

philosophy.believe: Never ask for anything you could remember or skip.
philosophy.guidance: Design the cancel step as a single tap with no reason prompt and no re-asking for details we already hold. Money rules (refund or credit around the cutoff) are not settled by this, so the team decides them and keeps them from slowing or complicating the cancel.
